name: Business Model Canvas
use_case: A single-page template that lays out how a venture creates, delivers and captures value across nine linked building blocks: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partners and cost structure. Best used when a new product, startup or internal venture needs its whole commercial logic visible at once, so the team can see which blocks are assumptions rather than facts and where the model breaks if one of them is wrong.
strengths: puts the entire commercial logic on one page a team can argue over
the links between blocks expose which assumptions the model depends on
fast enough to sketch several competing models and compare them
shared vocabulary across product, finance and sales
weaknesses: describes the model but does not test whether customers want it
no competitive dimension at all — pair it with an industry analysis
the one-page constraint hides operational detail that later matters
easy to fill in plausibly and mistake the artifact for validation
use_cases: A public agency redesigning a citizen service needs one page showing who the service is for, what it gives them, which partners it relies on and what it costs to run.
A charity whose main grant is ending wants to work out which of its activities could bring in income and what that would change about who it serves and what it depends on.
A university research group thinking about a spin-off has to lay out who would pay for its technology, how it would reach them, and what the company would need to own or build.
An established company whose core revenue is shrinking wants to sketch different ways of earning money from the customers and resources it already has, and compare them side by side.
